analysis.title: Boeing Co. (BA): The battle to get to normalized continues; Buy
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on BA after 3Q26 results (report dated 27 Oct 2026) and cuts the 12-month price target to $238 from $253. The stock closed at $168.18, which implies 41.5% upside.

GS says the 3Q26 update had incremental positives and negatives. Boeing still faces challenges in returning to normalized financial performance. Commercial aircraft demand is high, services is strong, defense revenue growth looks better after recent wins, and defense margins are inflecting.

Long-term commercial aircraft output and profitability likely have not changed, but the near-term ramp is shallower as Boeing works on supply chain and internal manufacturing. Near-term BCA margins are lower than GS expected.

Capex needs are higher for longer, partly for new business wins and partly to improve operations. Company capex assumptions for 2026-2029 are $4bn/5bn/4bn/4bn, and capex is likely to stay at 3-4% of revenue after that.

The 777X update was relatively positive and follows the MAX variant certifications, but the 777X development timeline still carries risk. 777-9 certification flight testing advanced and first delivery remains on track for 2027.
GS's view of normalized free cash flow has not changed in a while, but the time to reach it keeps moving.
3Q26 revenue was $24.19bn (up 4% y/y), above the FactSet figure of $23.95bn and GS's estimate of $23.66bn. Reported segment EBIT was $354mn versus GS's $577mn.

BCA operating income was $(697)mn versus GS's $(327)mn. GS attributes the miss to a less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs tied to production rate adjustments, and elevated supply chain costs. BCA revenue was $10.7bn, down 3.4% y/y.

BDS margin was 6.2% (3.0% excluding a $252mn gain on the HRL Laboratories sale) versus GS's 2.7% estimate. BDS revenue was $7.9bn, up 15% y/y on higher volume. BGS margin was 18.3% versus 17.5% a year ago, with revenue of $5.6bn, up 3.8% y/y.
3Q26 free cash flow was $464mn versus GS's estimate of $150mn and consensus of $330mn. Cash and equivalents were $20.7bn ($26.13 per share) and Boeing did not repurchase stock in the quarter.
Backlog: BCA backlog rose 2.5% sequentially to $611.8bn with a book-to-bill of 2.41X. BDS backlog rose 17.8% sequentially to $100.5bn with a book-to-bill of 2.9X.

Production: the 737 is progressing toward a stabilized 47/month and the 787 is stable at a build rate of 8/month. The 737-7 received amended type certification from the FAA in the quarter, followed by the 737-10 in October.

Boeing narrowed 2026 FCF guidance to ~$2bn (from $1-3bn) and gave 2027-2029 FCF guidance of about $3bn/6bn/10bn. The 2029 $10bn framework assumes mid-to-high 50s 737 MAX deliveries per month, about 12 per month on the 787, and a FCF-positive 777X program.

GS cut its 2026-2030E FCF/share estimates to $2.58/4.76/8.60/14.16/16.70 from $2.61/7.47/13.63/18.12/23.06. The price target now uses a 2.0% FCF yield on 2027E FCF (3.0% before), which equates to a 6% FCF yield on 2029E FCF of $10.9bn.
GS cut its EPS estimates to $(1.20) for 2026E, $3.14 for 2027E and $7.45 for 2028E. The previous figures were $0.39, $4.69 and $9.71.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and cuts the price target to $238 from $253 after 3Q26. The cut reflects lower FCF/share estimates from slower production rates, delivery timing, working capital and margins.

BA 3Q26 reported diluted EPS was $(0.15) versus a GS estimate of $0.21 and $(7.02) in 3Q25. Core EPS was $(0.34) versus a GS estimate of $0.05.
BA 3Q26 free cash flow was $464mn actual versus $150mn GS estimate and $330mn consensus. Full-year 2026 FCF guidance was narrowed to ~$2bn from $1-3bn, with 2027-2029 guidance of ~$3bn/6bn/10bn.
GS FY estimates: 2026E EPS $(1.20) new versus $0.39 old, 2027E EPS $3.14 new versus $4.69 old, 2028E EPS $7.45 new versus $9.71 old. 2026E revenue is $95.9bn, 2027E $108.8bn and 2028E $124.1bn.
risk_factors: Supply chain ability to ramp up production.
Contract operating performance within the defense segment.
The 777X development timeline still carries risk.
Higher capex for longer and a normalized FCF timeline that keeps moving.
